metric_rationale: The metric computes the proportion of choices that align with Tallying on the two most diagnostic trials (Trial 1 and Trial 2). In these trials, one option has 3 wins on low-validity features, while the other has 2 wins on high-validity features. Tallying purely counts wins, so it will strongly prefer the option with 3 wins. WADD weights by validity, so it will strongly prefer the option with 2 high-validity wins. Thus, Tallying predicts a value close to 1.0, whereas WADD predicts a value close to 0.0, providing maximal discrimination.

Focuses exclusively on the critical trial (Trial 1) designed to dissociate the two models. Tallying will consistently choose Option A (response 0) because it wins on more features. WADD will more frequently choose Option B (response 1) because the weighted sum of its two highly valid features typically exceeds the weighted sum of A's three less valid features. The mean response on this trial provides a massive and highly reliable contrast between the theories.

This metric calculates the proportion of times the subject chooses the option favored by the Weighted Additive (WADD) model over the option favored by the Take-The-Best (TTB) heuristic on the critical trials (Trials 1, 2, and 4). On these trials, TTB relies on the single most valid discriminating cue, whereas WADD integrates the remaining cues to override the best cue. The metric will be close to 0 for TTB and close to 1 for WADD.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the non-compensatory Take-The-Best (TTB) model on the most strongly diagnostic trials (Trial 1 and Trial 3). In these trials, a single highly valid cue favors one option while a coalition of several less valid cues favors the other. TTB predicts the single best cue will dominate, leading to a high proportion of choices for that option. WADD, being compensatory, integrates the multiple lower-validity cues which easily outweigh the single best cue, predicting the opposite choice. The difference in this proportion between the two models will be stark.

Calculates the difference in the probability of choosing Option A between Trial 2 and Trial 1. Strategy Mixture predicts a large positive difference because Tallying shifts from a tie (in Trial 1) to strongly favoring Option A (in Trial 2). In contrast, Noisy TTB predicts a difference near zero because the top two validities (0.9 and 0.85) dominate the noisy search in both trials, meaning the extra lower-tier features in Trial 2 rarely impact the decision.

This metric calculates the difference in the probability of choosing Option A between trials where Option A is supported by the highly diagnostic top feature (validity 0.95) versus trials where Option A is supported by the second-best feature (validity 0.75). According to the Strategy Mixture model, TTB strongly prefers A in both cases and Tallying strongly prefers B in both cases, leading to a similar mixture probability and a difference near zero. In contrast, Noisy TTB predicts a large difference because the 0.95 validity is robust to noise, whereas the 0.75 validity frequently swaps ranks with the closely clustered lower validities, leading to fewer choices of Option A in the second condition.
